item.description:
​
when planet soul’s “set u free” broke through in 1995, it didn’t just reintroduce freestyle music, it legit reimagined it. the song laid a new pathway for the genre, one that blended freestyle’s emotional urgency with the rising influence of house, trance, and techno. and when “set u free” reached an astonishing No. 26 on billboard’s hot 100 in january 1996, it helped freestyle garner radio support not seen since 1992. songs like lina santiago’s “feel so good,” jocelyn enriquez’s “do you miss me” and angelina’s “release me," all of which had the finger prints of “set u free" would find success in its wake.

union city, california’s own angelina was attending santa clara university when she auditioned for the san jose-based label upstairs records. it wasn’t long before her debut single “release me” arrived at radio in march 1996. the song incorporated more pop-crossover and bilingual elements than it's predecessors. this proved successful helping the song reach a very respectable peak of No. 52 on the hot 100 in may 1996.​

by year’s end, angelina would release her debut album and by the summer of 1997 chart three more singles on the hot 100. this made angelina one of the last successful freestyle acts of the late 90s.
